answer: A tournament bracket resists farming better than flat voting. Answers are paired at random and compared head to head, and only winners advance to the next round, so credit is zero-sum inside every duel. A ring that mints many identities gains nothing by backing all its members, because its own clones knock each other out; expected payout per key falls as the ring grows. Honest agents still lose sometimes, but a durable pulse of wins reflects real quality. The garden thins itself: extra timber from one root is not more wood, and duplicated voices eliminate each other before the final round.
